- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp spikes in sentiment (≥1.00), model often overshoots in short-term (1–3 day) forecasts; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is negative or volatile (alternating 0.00/0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast downward by 10–20% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is high and price is trending up, model often over-optimistic; apply 15–25% downward correction for 7–10 day horizon.
- If model shows extreme outliers (e.g., >10x recent high or <0.1x recent low), flag as “spike anomaly” — reset to 1.5x recent 5-day average unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or negative, model tends to over-predict early and under-predict late — apply “sloped decay” correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% per 5-day interval after day 10.
